DWR Application Modernization and Integration
SUMMARYOF FUNDS	FY 2025	FY 2026
	Actual	Estimate

FOOTNOTES
	FY 2025	FY 2026
SUMMARY OFFUNDS	Actual	Estimate

FOOTNOTES

1/ General Fund monies are transferred into the Automation Projects Fund to finance certain projects. See Table 2 for all fund transfers into the APF. These individual transfers are discussed in the narrative as part of the individual projects listed in the Automation Projects Fund.

2/ Represents expenditures from the APF. Because many of the APF appropriations are spent over multiple years, the FY 2025 actual column also includes non-lapsing expenditures from prior year appropriations.

3/ The monies appropriated in this subsection shall be spent for an integrated tax system modernization project that meets the following minimum specifications:

1. Captures data fields from electronically-filed individual and corporate income tax returns and makes the data available for querying and reporting purposes. The system shall provide the department of revenue staff, the joint legislative budget committee staff and governor's office of strategic planning and budgeting staff direct access to the querying and reporting functions. The querying and reporting functions shall include procedures to protect taxpayer confidentiality under applicable state and federal law.

2. For electronic corporate income tax returns, captures information regarding the principal business activity of the corporation. This requirement may be satisfied through North American industry classification system data listed on federal tax forms. The tax system shall allow for querying and reporting based on principal business activity.

FOOTNOTES

3. Includes an integrated individual income tax model within the project and provides the department of revenue staff, the joint legislative budget committee staff and governor's office of strategic planning and budgeting staff direct access to the individual income tax model. At a minimum, the model shall allow the department of revenue staff, the joint legislative budget committee staff and governor's office of strategic planning and budgeting staff to adjust tax law parameters against an anonymized representative sample of income tax returns to estimate the fiscal impact of proposed tax legislation. The model shall only include data from state and federal tax returns that are captured by the tax system. The individual income tax model shall include procedures to protect taxpayer confidentiality under applicable state and federal law.

4. Makes individual and corporate income tax data available for querying, modeling and reporting within twenty-four months following the end of a tax year. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

4/ The amounts appropriated pursuant to this section from the automation projects fund established by section 41-714, Arizona Revised Statutes, in fiscal year 2026-2027 are exempt from the provisions of section 35-190, Arizona Revised Statutes, relating to lapsing of appropriations, until June 30, 2028. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

5/ Within thirty days after the last day of each calendar quarter, the department of administration shall submit to the joint legislative budget committee a quarterly report on implementing projects approved by the information technology authorization committee established by section 18-121, Arizona Revised Statutes, including the projects' expenditures to date, deliverables, timeline for completion and current status. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

FOOTNOTES

6/ The transfers into the automation projects fund established by section 41-714, Arizona Revised Statutes, are not appropriations out of the automation projects fund. Only direct appropriations out of the automation projects fund are appropriations. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

Background

The APF is administered by ADOA and consists of subaccounts used to implement, upgrade, or maintain automation and information technology (IT) projects for state agencies. Pursuant to A.R.S. § 41-714, before monies are expended from the fund, ADOA must submit to the Joint Legislative Budget Committee (JLBC) for review an expenditure plan that includes project costs, deliverables, timeline for completion and method of procurement.

Pursuant to A.R.S. § 18-121, the Information Technology Authorization Committee (ITAC) is required to approve or disapprove all IT projects that exceed a total cost of \$1,000,000. If project costs are greater than \$5,000,000, A.R.S. § 18-104 requires an additional third-party analysis before receiving ITAC approval and requires agencies to submit quarterly progress reports from the third-party consultant. Unless otherwise noted, appropriations are non-lapsing for 2 years.

Department of Administration Subaccount

ADOA A to Z Arizona State Services Access Portal

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the A to Z Arizona State Services Access Portal. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Project Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(3,370,000) from the Department of Administration APF Subaccount in FY 2027 to eliminate one-time funding for the A to Z Arizona portal.

The portal will serve as a central hub for the public to access all state services. The portal will offer full selfservice to clients, expedite application vetting and processing, and reduce redundancies arising from the existence of multiple, independent client-facing portals. The portal will include additional data consolidation and identity verification features to reduce fraud.

The FY 2026 budget included an appropriation of \$3,370,000 for the project, financed from the State Web Portal Fund.

ADOA State Web Portal Software and Security Upgrades

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for State Web Portal Software and Security Upgrades. Adjustments are as follows:

text:
Remove One-Time Project Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(375,000) from the Department of Administration APF Subaccount in FY 2027 to eliminate one-time funding for software and security upgrades to the State Web Portal.

The State Web Portal hosts approximately 758,000 transactions per year among state, local, and municipal governments and members of the public. The upgrades to the portal will address security vulnerabilities in the current software to ensure future transactions can be completed safely and efficiently.

The FY 2026 budget included an appropriation of \$375,000 for the project, financed from the State Web Portal Fund.

ADOA State Website Migrations

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for State Website Migrations. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Project Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(1,750,000) from the ADOA APF Subaccount in FY 2027 to eliminate one-time funding for the migration various state websites to a new software platform.

There are currently 185 state agency websites hosted using the ADOA Agency Platform service. The software underlying the current version of this service stopped receiving maintenance and security updates in January 2025, which means that websites need to be migrated to a new platform or be left open to security risks. As of January 2025, ADOA had already migrated most of the 185 websites to a new version of the platform. The FY 2026 budget included an appropriation of \$1,750,000 for the project, financed from the Information Technology Fund, which will be used to migrate approximately 50 remaining websites.

ADOA K-12 School Financial Transparency Reporting Portal

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the K-12 School Financial Transparency Reporting Portal. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026. (Please see the FY 2026 Appropriations Report for additional background on the project.)

text:
ADOA HRIS Replacement

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the HRIS Replacement project. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Project Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(5,941,700) from the HRIS APF Subaccount in FY 2027 to eliminate one-time funding for the HRIS replacement project.

The FY 2026 budget included an appropriation of \$5,941,700 for the project, financed from the Information Technology Fund. (Please see the FY 2026 Appropriations Report for additional information.)

ADOA Business One-Stop Portal

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the Business One-Stop Portal. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Project Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(1,700,000) from the Business One-Stop APF Subaccount in FY 2027 to eliminate one-time funding for the Business One-Stop portal.

The FY 2023 budget included \$15,614,300 from the ADOA APF Subaccount in FY 2023 for the Business One-Stop Shop Web Portal. The FY 2023 funding was intended to add new functionalities to the Business One Stop portal and was financed from the General Fund.

At its June 2023 meeting, the JLBC gave a favorable review of ADOA's request to spend \$6,500,000 of its FY 2023 appropriation for FY 2024 operating costs and development of the Business One Stop portal. ADOA did not request approval for the remaining \$9,114,300, as separate projects within the Corporation Commission (e-Corp) and the Department of Revenue (AZTaxes) would have made some of the proposed Business One Stop portal features unnecessary.

The FY 2025 General Appropriations Act transferred \$7,000,000 from the ADOA APF Subaccount to the General Fund in FY 2024 and extended the lapsing date of the remaining \$2,114,300 through FY 2025 for maintenance and operations costs.

Since these monies lapsed, the FY 2026 budget appropriated \$2,114,300 from the Information Technology Fund to the Department of Administration for ongoing support of the Business One-Stop Portal.

The FY 2026 budget included an additional appropriation of \$1,700,000 for the project, financed from the Information Technology Fund. While prior appropriations were deposited into an ADOA APF subaccount, the FY 2026 appropriation was deposited into a new Business One-Stop APF subaccount.

Agriculture IT Projects and Cloud Migration

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for IT projects and cloud migration at the Department of Agriculture. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

The FY 2023 budget appropriated \$2,000,000 to the department to continue its efforts to modernize its IT systems and move the systems to the cloud. The FY 2023 appropriation was financed from the General Fund. At its December 2022 meeting, the JLBC gave a favorable review of the department's \$300,000 expenditure plan to conduct a feasibility study for the project. The Committee included a provision that required the department to report to the JLBC staff on the outcome of the feasibility study.

In November 2023, the department issued a task order to procure a cloud-based system based on the feasibility study roadmap. The project will be completed about 18 months after contract is awarded to the winning bidder.

The FY 2025 budget extended the lapsing date of the FY 2023 appropriation through FY 2026, and the FY 2026 budget further extended this lapsing date through FY 2027. In lieu of a meeting of the Joint Legislative Budget Committee, the FY 2026 budget also included a provision deeming the department's expenditure plan for the remaining \$1,700,000 of the FY 2023 appropriation as having been favorably reviewed by the Committee.

text:
AHCCCS Statewide HHIS Technology Projects

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for Statewide HHIS Technology Projects. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

The FY 2024 budget appropriated \$15,000,000 from the General Fund for Statewide HHIS Technology Projects. The appropriation was financed from the General Fund. The FY 2025 budget reduced the FY 2024 appropriation by \$(1,800,000) and specified that, of the remaining amount:

\$6,700,000 shall be used for a new information technology platform to authenticate individuals applying for health and human service programs to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse. The FY 2026 budget exempted this allocation from lapsing through FY 2026.

\$2,814,600 shall be used for the development of several modules associated with the Medicaid Enterprise System (MES) mainframe replacement. This project was deemed to have been favorably reviewed by JLBC in the FY 2025 budget so as to prevent a delay in proceeding with the project.

\$1,685,400 shall be used for MES fraud and waste abuse prevention enhancements. This project was deemed to have been favorably reviewed by JLBC in the FY 2025 budget so as to prevent a delay in proceeding with the project. This funding was moved to its own subaccount. Please see the next section \$2,000,000 shall be used for the MES Systems Integrator and ServiceNow projects. This project had already been favorably reviewed by the JLBC at its June 2023 meeting.

The AHCCCS project includes \$7,500,000 in federal expenditure authority from its operating budget.

Medicaid Enterprise System Mainframe Modernization

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the MES Mainframe Modernization. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Project Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(1,800,000) from the MES Modernization Subaccount in FY 2027 to eliminate one-time funding for the MES Mainframe Modernization project.

The FY 2024 budget included \$13,200,000 for Statewide HHIS Technology Projects (see above). Of this amount, \$2,814,600 was dedicated to the MES Mainframe Modernization project. The FY 2025 budget established a separate subaccount for this project and provided an appropriation of \$3,396,000. The FY 2026 budget included an additional appropriation of \$1,800,000 for the project, financed from the General Fund.

AHCCCS currently utilizes a mainframe-based application to support its core business operations. The mainframebased Prepaid Medical Management Information System (PMMIS) was developed using a now-outdated coding standard. The primary objective of the MES Mainframe Modernization is to migrate the AHCCCS mainframe system to the cloud.

The total project budget is estimated to be \$114,323,833. Of this amount, state costs are \$13,405,431. The remaining amount will come from federal funds and the state of Hawaii, which currently shares Medicaid systems with AHCCCS.

Corporation Commission Online Records & Filing System

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for an Online Records and Filing System Replacement project. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

The Corporation Commission e-Corp system provides online access to corporation and limited liability company records on file with the agency's Corporations Division. The vendor stopped maintaining the current system in FY 2024. The FY 2024 budget included \$7,000,000 from the Corporation Commission APF Subaccount to implement and migrate to a new cloud-based system. The FY 2024 appropriation was financed by a transfer from the Securities Regulatory and Enforcement Fund. The FY 2026 budget exempted the FY 2024 appropriation from lapsing through FY 2026.

text:
Judiciary Community Supervision Electronic Monitoring

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the Statewide Community Supervision Electronic Monitoring System. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

In FY 2023, the Supreme Court initiated a \$2,500,000 pilot project funded with the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA)

Funds. The system is designed to enable probation officers to monitor and communicate with individuals involved in the criminal justice system, both pre-trial and in selected probation groups, using a cell phone. The FY 2024 budget included \$2,500,000 from the Judiciary Supreme Court APF Subaccount to continue the project. The FY 2024 appropriation was financed from the General Fund. At its October 2023 meeting, the JLBC gave a favorable review of the project which is expected to be completed in FY 2027.

The FY 2025 budget extended the lapsing date of the FY 2024 appropriation through FY 2027.

Judiciary Probation Case Management System

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 to replace the Probation Case Management System. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026. (Please see the FY 2026 Appropriations Report for additional background on the project.)

DPS Concealed Weapons Tracking System

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for upgrades to the Department of Public Safety (DPS) Concealed Weapons Tracking System. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

The FY 2022 budget included \$550,000 from the DPS APF Subaccount to complete upgrades to the Concealed Weapons Tracking System. The FY 2024 budget included an additional \$494,500 for the same purpose. The FY 2026 budget exempted the FY 2024 appropriation from lapsing through FY 2026.

The system tracks concealed weapon permits and allows law enforcement to verify permits. The current system uses antiquated mainframe technology. The new system will interface with other law enforcement systems and allow the public to renew permits online. (Please see the FY 2022 Appropriations Report for additional background on the project.)

Real Estate Department Subaccount

Real Estate Department System Modernization

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the Real Estate Department System Modernization Project. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Project Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(1,962,000) from the Real Estate Department APF Subaccount to eliminate onetime funding for the Real Estate Department System Modernization project.

The IT system currently used by the department was developed by a single employee who still maintains the system to this day, but who is set to retire before the end of FY 2026. The FY 2025 budget included a footnote allowing the department to use up to \$400,000 of its operating appropriation to begin planning for the system’s replacement. The FY 2026 budget included an appropriation of \$1,962,000 for the project, financed from the General Fund. The FY 2026 appropriation is expected to sufficiently fund the entirety of the new IT system’s development. After the project is completed, ongoing licensing costs and user fees are expected to be approximately \$850,000 per year.

DOR Integrated Tax System Modernization

The Baseline includes \$19,756,800 in FY 2027 for the DOR's development of a new integrated tax system. Adjustments are as follows:

FY 2027 Development Costs

The Baseline includes a one-time increase of \$19,756,800 from the DOR APF Subaccount in FY 2027 for the continuation of the DOR Integrated Tax System Modernization project. The FY 2027 funding level is included in the FY 2026 budget's 3-year General Fund spending plan, which is reflected in Table 1.

The FY 2027 appropriation will be financed by a transfer from the following funds to the DOR APF Subaccount:

• \$12,538,400 from the General Fund

\$7,218,400 from the Integrated Tax System Project Fund. The Integrated Tax System Fund consists of monies recovered from local governments (including regional transportation authorities) and state non-General Fund accounts that will benefit from the system.

As part of the FY 2023 budget, DOR estimated that the system will cost \$104,827,600 to implement by FY 2028. The long-term spending plan for the tax system assumed that development costs would be allocated as follows: 1) 60.89% from the General Fund; 2) 34.06% from Local Governments; 3) 4.13% from the 0.6% Education Sales Tax; and 4) 0.92% from the 16% recreational marijuana excise tax. As noted above, the non-General Fund sources (which total 39.11% of the project budget) are deposited into the Integrated Tax System Project Fund.

Given these fixed allocation percentages, of the total project budget of \$104,827,600, the General Fund cost would be \$63,829,700. The remaining \$40,997,900 is to be appropriated from the Integrated Tax System Project Fund as shown in Table 1.

The FY 2025 3-year spending plan included \$19,256,800 for the project in FY 2026. However, the project is currently behind schedule and is no longer expected to be complete by FY 2028. As a result of this delay, the FY 2026 budget included no funding for the project in FY 2026 and instead shifted the amount previously allocated in FY 2026 to FY 2029. The FY 2026 budget also exempted the FY 2024 appropriation from lapsing through FY 2026. Table 1 has been updated to reflect the new annual funding schedule.

FY 2027 Development Costs

DOR is given annual guidance in budget legislation on the dollar amounts of these non-General Fund allocations, which represent the fixed percentages multiplied by that year's annual project budget. In addition, budget legislation also provides DOR guidance for the assessment of the local government charges. Given the lack of any General Fund contribution in FY 2026, the FY 2026 Revenue BRB suspended the local cost contribution as well. (Please see the FY 2025 Appropriations Report for more historical background on this project.)
